extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (computational number theorists, mathematicians, and programmers using the PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions (number theory, quadratic forms, Dirichlet characters, discrete logs, polynomials). For each function the page gives purpose, complexity, warnings, examples and library syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbclassno(D, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary class number of the quadratic order of discriminant D, for "small" values of D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If D>0 or flag=1: uses O(|D|^{1/2}) algorithm (compute L(1,χ_D) with approximate functional equation) — slower than quadclassunit for |D| ≈ 10^2 and not meant for large D. If D<0 and flag=0 (or omitted): uses O(|D|^{1/4}) Shanks baby-step/giant-step method — faster for small |D| (say |D|<10^18). Important warning: this implementation is a partial Shanks method and is unconditionally correct for |D| < 2·10^{10} but may be incorrect for larger |D| if the class group has many cyclic factors; recommended to double-check with quadclassunit (which is 2–3× slower in |D|∈[10^{10},10^{18}] assuming GRH). Note: does not compute number of classes of primitive binary forms (narrow class number) for D>0 when fundamental unit has positive norm; see QFBclassno formula to convert. Examples and library syntax: GEN qfbclassno0(GEN D, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbcompraw(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of binary quadratic forms x and y without reduction of the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to compute generating element of an ideal. Result undefined if x and y don't have the same discriminant. Library syntax: GEN qfbcompraw(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbhclassno(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurwitz class number H(x): defined for x non-negative and ≡ 0 or 3 (mod 4), 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For x>5·10^5 the function assumes GRH and uses quadclassunit with default params. Examples show small values (e.g., H(3)=1/3, H(4)=1/2). Library syntax: GEN hclassno(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnucomp(x, y, L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms x and y using Shanks' NUCOMP and NUDUPL algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: L is any positive constant, optimal speed when L = |D/4|^{1/4} (sqrt-nint(abs(D)>>2,4)), where D is common discriminant. Result undefined if discriminants differ. Current implementation slower than generic routine for small D; becomes faster for D of about 45 bits. Library syntax: GEN nucomp(GEN x, GEN y, GEN L). Also nudupl for x=y.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnupow(x, n, {L})
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of primitive positive definite binary quadratic form x using NUCOMP/NUDUPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If L set, should equal sqrt-nint(abs(D)>>2,4) where D<0 is discriminant. Implementation slower for small discriminant and becomes faster for D ≈ 2^{45}. Library syntax: GEN nupow(GEN x, GEN n, GEN L = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbpowraw(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of binary quadratic form x computed without reduction (via qfbcompraw).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n must be non-negative and n < 2^{31}. Library syntax: GEN qfbpowraw(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbprimeform(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prime binary quadratic form of discriminant x whose first coefficient is p (|p| prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: p = ±1 returns the unit form. Returns error if x not quadratic residue mod p or if x<0 and p<0 (negative definite t_QFI not implemented). For x>0, distance component set to zero per current precision. Library syntax: GEN primeform(GEN x, GEN p, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbred(x, {flag = 0}, {d}, {isd}, {sd})
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduces binary quadratic form x (updates Shanks' distance function if x is indefinite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag bits: 1 = perform single reduction step; 2 = don't update Shanks' distance. Optional d, isd, sd supply discriminant and its square-root values (no checking). If d<0 square-root fields irrelevant. Multiple convenience aliases exist (redimag for definite x; redreal, rhoreal, redrealnod, rhorealnod for indefinite forms). Library syntax: GEN qfbred0(GEN x, long flag, GEN d = NULL, GEN isd = NULL, GEN sd = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbredsl2(x, {data})
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction of (real or imaginary) binary quadratic form x returning [y,g] where y is reduced and g ∈ SL(2,Z) with g·x = y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: data, if given, must equal [D, sqrtint(D)] where D>0 is discriminant. Distance component unaffected for t_QFR. Library syntax: GEN qfbredsl2(GEN x, GEN data = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbsolve(Q, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve Q(x,y)=p over integers where Q is a binary quadratic form and p a prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns [x,y] (one solution) or 0 if none. Algorithm is probabilistic poly-time in p (square root of D mod p). Polynomial in D if Q imaginary; exponential in D if Q real (requires full cycle of reduced forms). For real Q, bnfisprincipal can give solution in heuristic subexponential time assuming GRH. Library syntax: GEN qfbsolve(GEN Q, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadclassunit(D, {flag = 0}, {tech = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Buchmann-McCurley sub-exponential algorithm for computing class group of quadratic order of discriminant D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be used instead of qfbclassno or quadregula when D < −10^{25}, D > 10^{10}, or when group structure is wanted. Returns vector v with v.no (class number), v.cyc (structure as product of cyclic groups), v.gen (generators as binary quadratic forms), v.reg (regulator with computed accuracy). Flag obsolete. Optional tech = [c1,c2] controls execution time/stack, balancing relation finding vs linear algebra: increasing c1 makes relations easier to find but requires more relations and heavier linear algebra. Default c2 chosen to be provably correct under GRH (Bach's bound c2=6 noted). Use GEN Buchquad for experimenting with tech parameter. If only class number needed, quadclassno(GEN D) is faster (assuming GRH). For negative D with |D|<10^{20}, qfbclassno might be faster but may be wrong. Library syntax: GEN quadclassunit0(GEN D, long flag, GEN tech = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quaddisc(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminant of the étale algebra Q(√x): returns 0 for x=0, 1 for x a square, otherwise discriminant of the quadratic field Q(√x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes by stripping square factors x = d f^2 with d square-free integer. Examples: quaddisc(7)=28, quaddisc(-7)=-7. Library syntax: GEN quaddisc(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadgen(D, {v = 'w'})
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates quadratic number ω = (a + √D)/2 with a=0 if D≡0 mod4, a=1 if D≡1 mod4, so (1,ω) is integral basis for quadratic order of discriminant D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D must be integer ≡0 or 1 mod4 and not a square. Optional v chooses display variable. Errors on square discriminant. Library syntax: GEN quadgen0(GEN D, long v = -1) and GEN quadgen(GEN D).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadhilbert(D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative equation defining the Hilbert class field of quadratic field of discriminant D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If D<0 uses complex multiplication (Schertz variant). If D>0 uses Stark units and may return vector of extensions whose compositum is the class field in rare cases; see bnrstark for details. Library syntax: GEN quadhilbert(GEN D, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadpoly(D, {v = 'x'})
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates canonical quadratic polynomial (in variable v) corresponding to discriminant D (minimal polynomial of quadgen(D)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D must be integer ≡0 or 1 mod4 and not a square. Errors on square discriminant. Library syntax: GEN quadpoly0(GEN D, long v = -1) and GEN quadpoly(GEN D).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadray(D, f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative equation for ray class field of conductor f for quadratic field of discriminant D using analytic methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For D<0 uses σ function and Schertz method. For D>0 uses Stark's conjecture and may return vector of relative equations; see bnrstark for details. Accepts bnf for x^2 - D too. Library syntax: GEN quadray(GEN D, GEN f, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadregulator(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulator of quadratic field of positive discriminant x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns error if x not a discriminant or if x is a square. For large x see quadclassunit. Library syntax: GEN quadregulator(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadunit(D, {v = 'w'})
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental unit u of real quadratic field Q(√D) where D positive discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If D not fundamental discriminant probably returns unit of corresponding order. D must be integer ≡0 or 1 mod4 and not a square. Optional v chooses display variable. Library syntax: GEN quadunit0(GEN D, long v = -1) and GEN quadunit(GEN D).

rubrics_metrics.name: ramanujantau(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Ramanujan's tau function τ(n) at an individual n (assuming GRH for speedups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm complexity ~ Õ(n^{1/2}) time and O(log n) space. If all values up to N required, computing q*eta(q+O(q^N))^24 and vectorization (tauvec) gives Õ(N) time and Õ(N) space, faster than repeated calls. Examples show using tauvec for bulk computation is much faster. Library syntax: GEN ramanujantau(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: randomprime({N = 2^31})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a strong pseudoprime in [2, N-1] (or a pseudoprime in given interval [a,b]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If upper bound < 2^64 returned pseudoprime is proven prime. If interval provided and no prime exists, function may loop infinitely. Library syntax: GEN randomprime(GEN N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: removeprimes({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes primes listed in x from the extra prime table (undo addprimes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x omitted lists current extra primes. x can be single integer or vector. Example: removeprimes(addprimes()) empties extra prime table. Library syntax: GEN removeprimes(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: sigma(x, {k = 1}) (sumdivk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of k-th powers of positive divisors of |x| (x and k integers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also available as sumdiv for k=1. Library syntax: GEN sumdivk(GEN x, long k) and GEN sumdiv(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtint(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integer square root: largest integer y with y^2 ≤ x for non-negative integer x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows difference from floating sqrt. Library syntax: GEN sqrtint(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtnint(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integer n-th root: largest integer y with y^n ≤ x for non-negative integer x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special case n=2 is sqrtint. Library syntax: GEN sqrtnint(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdedekind(h, k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns Dedekind sum s(h,k) = sum_{n=1}^{k-1} (n/k)*(frac(h*n/k) - 1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides fast implementation for Dedekind sums. Library syntax: GEN sumdedekind(GEN h, GEN k).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdigits(n, {B = 10})
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of digits of integer n in base B>1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sumdigits(123456789)=45; for base 2 it returns Hamming weight. Faster than vecsum(digits(n,B)) when B=10 or power of 2; only slightly faster otherwise. Library syntax: GEN sumdigits0(GEN n, GEN B = NULL) and GEN sumdigits(GEN n) for B=10.

rubrics_metrics.name: znchar(D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given datum D describing group (Z/NZ)^* and Dirichlet character χ, return pair [G, chi] where G is znstar(N,1) and chi is GP character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D can be integer discriminant (return Kronecker real character), Mod(m,N) (Conrey character), modular form space mfinit([N,k,χ]) or modular form (extract underlying Dirichlet character). Other supported formats: [G,chi] pair input returns same. Several examples show usage and conversion; library syntax: GEN znchar(GEN D).

rubrics_metrics.name: zncharconductor(G, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return conductor of Dirichlet character chi on (Z/qZ)^* (G = znstar(q,1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns primitive conductor (t_INT bid.mod) if chi primitive; otherwise returns [N, factor(N)]. Examples show trivial and non-trivial characters. Library syntax: GEN zncharconductor(GEN G, GEN chi).

rubrics_metrics.name: znchardecompose(G, chi, Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose Dirichlet character χ into local characters χ_p modulo N where p|(Q,N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given G=znstar(N,1), chi and integer Q, returns decomposition χ = ∏ χ_p with conductors dividing p^{e_p}. Example: decomposition into p=2 and p=5 parts in modulus 40. Returns Conrey char (t_COL) for the local parts. Library syntax: GEN znchardecompose(GEN G, GEN chi, GEN Q).

rubrics_metrics.name: znchargauss(G, chi, {a = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute complex Gauss sum g(χ,a) = sum_{n=1}^N χ(n) e(an/N) for Dirichlet character χ on G=(Z/NZ)^*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: quadratic Gauss sums give i*sqrt(3) etc. Precision and normalization issues demonstrated; library syntax: GEN znchargauss(GEN G, GEN chi, GEN a = NULL, long bitprec).

rubrics_metrics.name: zncharinduce(G, chi, N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given chi modulo q (G = znstar(q,1)), induce chi to modulus N (multiple of q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N can be integer, factorization matrix, pair [N,factor(N)], or znstar(N,1). Works with Conrey labels or vectors; examples show inducing trivial/non-trivial chars and interplay with znchartoprimitive. Library syntax: GEN zncharinduce(GEN G, GEN chi, GEN N).

rubrics_metrics.name: zncharisodd(G, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return 1 iff chi(-1) = -1 (odd character), else 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts character as t_VEC, t_INT or t_COL (Conrey index/log). Examples provided. Library syntax: long zncharisodd(GEN G, GEN chi).

rubrics_metrics.name: znchartokronecker(G, chi, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: If chi is real and equals Kronecker symbol (D/·), return discriminant D (flag=0) or fundamental discriminant attached to primitive character (flag=1); otherwise return 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discriminant is fundamental iff chi primitive. Examples with characters mod 8 demonstrate outputs. Library syntax: GEN znchartokronecker(GEN G, GEN chi, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: znchartoprimitive(G, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given chi modulo q (G=znstar(q,1)) with conductor q0|q, return [G0, chi0] where chi0 is primitive character and G0 describes modulus q0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show trivial/non-primitive characters being reduced to modulus 1 and empty character. Note znconreyconductor can be more efficient for getting conductor and chi0 without initializing G0. Library syntax: GEN znchartoprimitive(GEN G, GEN chi).

rubrics_metrics.name: znconreychar(G, m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return Dirichlet character attached to m ∈ (Z/qZ)^* via Conrey's logarithm, expressed in standard PARI form in terms of SNF generators G.gen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents Conrey generators gp for each prime divisor and special treatment for p=2 (g4,g8), the Conrey logarithm vector (mp)_p∈S_q and relation to Conrey exp/log utilities. Examples illustrate characters for (Z/8Z)^* and error handling for non-coprime inputs. Library syntax: GEN znconreychar(GEN G, GEN m) and accepts Conrey log as input.

rubrics_metrics.name: znconreyconductor(G, chi, {&chi0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return conductor of chi; if primitive return t_INT bid.mod, otherwise return [N, factor(N)]. Optionally set chi0 to Conrey log of attached primitive character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More efficient than znchartoprimitive because it avoids initializing G0. Examples show retrieving primitive conductor 125 for a char mod 5^3 and obtaining chi0. Library syntax: GEN znconreyconductor(GEN G, GEN chi, GEN *chi0 = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: znconreyexp(G, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return integer m ∈ (Z/qZ)^* such that znconreylog(G,m) = chi (Conrey exponential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: chi can be t_VEC (generators G.gen) or t_COL (Conrey log). Examples demonstrate conversion between representations. Library syntax: GEN znconreyexp(GEN G, GEN chi).

rubrics_metrics.name: znconreylog(G, m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return Conrey logarithm of m ∈ (Z/qZ)^* relative to Conrey generators gp: vector (m_p)_p∈S_q giving discrete log coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines gp construction, special handling for 2, and conversion from SNF generators via ideallog. Errors for non-coprime inputs. Examples show conversion and interaction with znconreyexp and znconreychar. Library syntax: GEN znconreylog(GEN G, GEN m).

rubrics_metrics.name: zncoppersmith(P, N, X, {B = N})
rubrics_metrics.description: Find integers x with |x| ≤ X such that gcd(N, P(x)) ≥ B using Coppersmith's algorithm (LLL-based).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: X must be < exp(log2 B/(deg(P) log N)); for B=N this means X < N^{1/deg(P)}. Smaller B or larger X slows routine. Strength is finding roots modulo composite N; for prime/power N use polrootsmod or polrootspadic. Applications: factoring with partial info (recover p from last digits), small-exponent RSA attacks when message short and padding known. Examples provided with timings. Library syntax: GEN zncoppersmith(GEN P, GEN N, GEN X, GEN B = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: znlog(x, g, {o})
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete logarithm: two modes — if g is znstar output (initialized), compute discrete log of x w.r.t. generators in structure; else g is explicit element in (Z/NZ)^* and compute discrete log of x base g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns [] when x not a power of g (may enter infinite loop). Optional o represents multiplicative order of g (preferred [ord, factor(ord)]) for speedup. Uses combination of algorithms: Pohlig-Hellman to reduce, Shanks baby-step/giant-step for small q (<2^32), Pollard rho for large q, and index-calculus for prime N when feasible. Complexity caveats: Pollard rho may loop indefinitely when no solution. p-adic g allowed. Library syntax: GEN znlog0(GEN x, GEN g, GEN o = NULL) and GEN znlog(GEN x, GEN g, GEN o).

rubrics_metrics.name: znorder(x, {o})
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of x in multiplicative group (Z/nZ)^*; error if x not invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: o, if present, is non-zero multiple of order (preferred [ord,factor(ord)] where ord = eulerphi(n)) to speed computation. Library syntax: GEN znorder(GEN x, GEN o = NULL) and alias GEN order(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: znprimroot(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return primitive root (generator) of (Z/nZ)^* when that group is cyclic (n=4 or n=2 p^k or n=p^k where p odd prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If group not cyclic result undefined. For prime powers returns smallest positive primitive root (exception noted for 2 p^k). Requires factoring p-1 for prime p which may be costly. Library syntax: GEN znprimroot(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: znstar(n, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives structure of multiplicative group (Z/nZ)^*. Returns G depending on flag: flag=0 returns abelian group structure [h,d,g] with h=φ(n), d vector of invariant factors, g generators; flag=1 returns bid structure allowing discrete log computations (znlog).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides convenience values G.no, G.cyc, G.gen. Defines znstar(0) as [2,[2],[-1]] (Z^*). Library syntax: GEN znstar0(GEN n, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: O(p^e) / ggrando / zeropadic / zeroser
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct p-adic or power series zero objects of given precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p integer > 2 returns p-adic 0 of precision e; otherwise returns power series zero with precision given by ev, where v is X-adic valuation of p. Library syntaxes: GEN ggrando(), GEN zeropadic(GEN p, long e) for p-adic, GEN zeroser(long v, long e) for power series zero in variable v.

rubrics_metrics.name: bezoutres(A, B, {v}) (polresultantext alias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias for polresultantext (polynomial resultant extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polresultantext0(GEN A, GEN B, long v = -1) where v is a variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: deriv(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivative of x with respect to main variable (or v if provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivative of scalar is zero; vector/matrix derivative componentwise. For t_POLMOD main variable is chosen among coefficients' main variables; mute variable X treated accordingly. Shortcut x' available. Library syntax: GEN deriv(GEN x, long v = -1) where v is variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: diffop(x, v, d, {n = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply n-th power of differential operator D specified by variables v and their values d to x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: v is vector of variables, d vector same length giving D values. Applies componentwise; for t_POLMOD if modulus variable value missing it is derived via implicit function theorem. Examples: differentiation of formal expressions (e.g., exp(X^2)), use to compute Bell polynomials via Faà di Bruno. Library syntax: GEN diffop0(GEN x, GEN v, GEN d, long n). For n=1 GEN diffop(GEN x, GEN v, GEN d) available.

rubrics_metrics.name: eval(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace formal variables in x by values assigned after creation; if x is string execute it as GP command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainly useful in GP interactive mode (not library). Distinct from subst (substitution). Examples show evaluating constructed variable names and executing command strings. Library syntax: eval(x) in GP; behavior described.
